court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Jalgaon (CRIMINAL REVISION APPLICATION NO. 369 OF 2003)
case_name: Sk Rauf Sk Usman & Anr vs State Of Maha

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sk. Rauf Sk. Usman, Labour; Masum Ali Sk. Buchanu, Labour

facts_of_case: After marriage, family members used to beat and illtreat prosecutrix and subjected her to cruelty on the ground of demand of Rs.10,000/- from her parents.

legal_principles.principle: The court's inherent powers cannot be used to quash proceedings in a case where the parties are governed by Muslim law and the offence is not compoundable.
legal_principles.held: Thus, this Court has no inherent powers to quash and set aside the proceedings as it is not compoundable under Section 320 Cr.P.Code.
cited_cases: Vasudeo K. Dalal Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2003) 2 B.Cr.C. 558
use_in: cases involving Muslim law and compoundable offences
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — one reason why the court's inherent powers are limited

legal_principles.principle: A compromise in a criminal case can be allowed if the parties agree to settle their dispute, but only for offences that are compoundable.
legal_principles.held: However, offence punishable under Sec. 323 I.P. Code is compoundable.
use_in: cases involving minor offences and willing parties
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — one reason why compromise is allowed in certain cases

outcome.final_order: Conviction under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code against the applicants is maintained.
